value.body: A web developer builds and maintains websites and web apps. IT service firms, product companies, agencies and many non-tech businesses hire them, and some work as freelancers. A typical day involves writing and testing code, fixing bugs, and working with designers and other developers.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BCA, B.Tech/B.E. or B.Sc (Computer Science/IT); a strong portfolio can also count

items.label: Common tools
items.value: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, a web framework, Git

items.label: Tech industry workforce
items.note: All tech roles, not only web developers

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually enter through campus placements, off-campus hiring tests or internships. Projects you can show, such as live websites or code on a public repository, often matter as much as the degree. Small firms and agencies are common first employers.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Building page layouts with HTML and CSS
Working with databases and server-side code

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: frontend, backend or full-stack developer, then senior or lead roles.
Tools change often, so continuous learning is part of the job.
Entry-level competition is high; a portfolio helps you stand out.
Freelance and remote work are possible.
